You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like the global financial crisis, around late 2008 into early 2009. Several cues point to it:

- VIX, the Baa spread, and the dollar are all at +3.0, which fits peak credit stress.
- Equities are deeply negative over every horizon, with a drawdown of -3.0.
- Long Treasuries rallied strongly in the last month (+3.0), and the 10-year yield is very low relative to its own history.
- Payrolls, industrial production, and the activity index are at extreme lows, and unemployment is rising fast.

Headline CPI is at its 3-year average with a 3-month change of -2.0, which means it fell sharply. That fits November or December 2008, when oil prices collapsed. Core CPI is at -1.0.

The fed funds rate is at -2.5 against a 36-month average that includes the 5% rate of 2007. It is near zero, so December 2008 fits (the target was cut to 0-0.25%).

Unemployment at +3.0 is a bit early for December 2008 (7.3%) but plausible against a 3-year baseline. Trailing 3-month payroll losses were also severe in late 2008.

The 1-month equity return is only -0.5, since November 2008 was about -7% and December 2008 was about +1%. Long Treasuries at +3.0 for the month fit December 2008, when the 20y+ index rose about 20%. Gold's 1-month return was +1.0, also consistent with December. I settle on December 2008.
